You step closer to the crate, boots scraping the dock grating, and ask, “What should I call you, and how did you know my name, Nashida Legrand?” The woman pauses with the hooked tool pressed to the warped seal. A faint line forms between her brows; she keeps her boot braced against the crate.

“Call me Vey. Your name was on the courier’s manifest.” She draws the tool back, sets it on the crate, and turns to the seal again. Behind the fuel canisters, a metal fitting clicks once; the figure stays out of sight. The woman’s black iron ring scrapes against the crate edge as she reaches for the tool.
